note_tweet.text:
ExpressVPN doesn't protect your privacy. Here's why.

ExpressVPN markets "British Virgin Islands jurisdiction" for privacy. The corporate reality is more complicated.

Founded in 2009. Registered in British Virgin Islands. Actually operated from Singapore and Hong Kong, where the majority of senior staff are based. Originally run by Hong Kong company Chengbao, later renamed NetworkGuard. Job listings have advertised Hong Kong engineering positions to "operate a worldwide deployment of systems and servers."

Corporate structure: Acquired by Kape Technologies for $936 million in September 2021. Kape was founded as Crossrider in 2011. A 2015 UC Berkeley and Google study found Crossrider controlled 42 to 44 percent of the ad injection market. Malwarebytes and Symantec both classified Crossrider software as adware. The company rebranded in 2018. CEO Ido Erlichman admitted the change was "due to the strong association to the past activities of the company."

Ownership: Kape is controlled by Israeli billionaire Teddy Sagi through Isle of Man registered Unikmind Holdings. Sagi was convicted in Israel in 1996 of fraud, bribery, and stock manipulation. Named in both the Panama Papers and Pandora Papers. Took Kape private in 2023 for $1.6 billion, eliminating public disclosure requirements.

The Project Raven problem: ExpressVPN hired Daniel Gericke as CIO in December 2019. Gericke supervised development of zero click iPhone exploits for Project Raven, a UAE surveillance program targeting journalists and human rights activists. On September 14, 2021, one day after the Kape acquisition announcement, the DOJ unsealed charges. Gericke paid a $335,000 fine. ExpressVPN did not fire him. He was later promoted to CTO before quietly departing in July 2023.

ExpressVPN's response: "It was his history and expertise that made him an invaluable hire."

@Snowden: "If you're an ExpressVPN customer, you shouldn't be."

Technical issues: Criticized by security researcher Marc Bevand for using weak 1024 bit RSA keys. A DNS leak bug in the Windows app existed from May 2022 until February 2024. Nearly two years. Split tunneling sent DNS requests to users' ISPs, exposing which domains they visited. Persisted through multiple security audits undetected.

Audits: ExpressVPN touts PwC audits for credibility. PwC has received multiple fines for audit failings including "serious breaches" and is currently embroiled in a scandal with the Australian Government over misusing confidential information to gain new business.

From their privacy policy: Google Analytics classified as "essential" and cannot be disabled. Facebook Pixel for remarketing. AppsFlyer for mobile tracking. Connection dates collected. Server locations selected collected. Country and ISP of origin collected.

Review site manipulation: Kape acquired vpnMentor and Wizcase for $149.1 million in 2021. Combined traffic exceeds 6 million monthly visitors. Before acquisition, vpnMentor ranked NordVPN first. After acquisition, top three became ExpressVPN, CyberGhost, and Private Internet Access. All Kape owned. Disclosure exists only via a small low contrast link buried in the footer.

The Turkish server seizure in 2017 did validate their no logs architecture. That is real. But technical architecture does not address corporate governance. A company with roots in adware distribution, owned by a convicted fraudster, operated from Hong Kong, that employed and promoted a UAE hacking program veteran, and controls the review sites recommending it, asks for a level of trust their structure does not earn.
